title: Discrete lattice derived invariants via a sheaf-module Koszul resolution
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $r\geq0$, and let $P$ be an internal $R$-module [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] equipped with pairwise commuting $R$-linear automorphisms $T_1,\ldots,T_r$. Equivalently $P$ has an action of the discrete group $D=\mathbf Z^r$, whose $i$th basis vector acts as $T_i$. Write $R\Gamma_D$ for the ordinary total right derived functor of invariants on $D$-equivariant internal $R$-modules. Define the cochain complex $K_R(P;T)$ in degrees $0,\ldots,r$ by
$$K_R(P;T)^a=\bigoplus_{I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\},\ |I|=a}P,\qquad (dx)_J=\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}(T_i-1)x_{J\setminus\{i\}}.$$
There is a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_R:K_R(P;T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_D(P)$$
in the ordinary derived category of internal $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Its map from $P^D[0]$ is the degree-zero inclusion of invariant elements into $K_R(P;T)^0=P$. For a morphism $\varphi:R\to R'$ of commutative condensed rings, an internal $R'$-module $P'$ with commuting automorphisms $T'_i$, and an $R$-linear equivariant morphism $f:P\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi P'$, the square with rows $\lambda_R,\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\lambda_{R'}$ and columns the termwise map induced by $f$ and the canonical derived coefficient map $R\Gamma_D(P)\to\operatorname{Res}_\varphi R\Gamma_D(P')$ commutes. For $r=0$, $\lambda_R$ is the identity $P[0]$.
